correctness.rationale: For c>xi the response (z+xi)/(z+c), z=x/(1+b x^2), is strictly increasing in z. With gamma=1/sqrt(b), the normalized response gap factors exactly as beta(c-xi)b(x-gamma)^2/[(1+2c sqrt(b))(c(1+b x^2)+x)]. This ensures predator monotonicity; positivity, logistic upper comparison and regularity give global bounded solutions. If y tends to a positive L, the response gap is integrable along the trajectory and uniformly continuous, hence tends to zero. Its only zero on the bounded prey range is gamma, where the limiting prey derivative would be -f(gamma)L<0, a contradiction. Once y tends to zero, comparing x with logistic equations of growth rates 1 and 1-epsilon gives x tending to gamma. The exact quotient w=(x-gamma)/y solves w'=-(x/gamma-a(x))w-f(x), where a is the gap; the coefficient tends to 1 and forcing to -F with F=f(gamma). A stable scalar variation-of-constants argument gives w tending to -F. With G=-g''(gamma)=2(c-xi)b^(3/2)/(1+2c sqrt(b))^2, the derivative of y^-2 tends to beta G F^2. Integrate and divide by t to recover both stated constants. The positive leading constants rule out exponential approach on these trajectories. Global means finite strictly positive initial densities, not the invariant x=0 or y=0 faces.
